results.title: How and Why to Take Manual Sounding On a Ship?
excerpts:
Sounding Table
Sounding table is a chart describing the construction, capacity and most importantly the volumetric content of the tank at given depth of sounding or ullage. All vessels have their own sounding table documents for each tank containing fluid in bulk.
The sounding table is compiled to show the volumetric quantity of fluid at various trims and list for the particular sounding depth in cm.
<Sounding Table>
Tape is rolled inside the tank till the bob touches the tank bottom. If the tape measure 1000 cm – check the list or trim of the ship and compare the volumetric value for the sounding depth of 1000 cm.
2. Measuring level by calculating the Ullage of the tank
This method is convenient if the fluid in the tank is at a higher level. In heavy oil tanks and viscous fluids, this method does not spoil the whole sounding tape and avoids a false reading.
<Sounding Table>
For e.g. If the sounding tape is lowered till 500 cm and the tape measures oil in the tape as 100 cm.
The total depth of the sounding pipe is 1600 cm. Hence the ullage is: 500cm- 100cm= 400cm, and sounding value can be calculated as
1600 – 500 +100 = 1200 cm.
Normally ullage values are also provided in the sounding table with reference to the trim of the ship to get the volumetric content in the tank.

Planning estimate. Verify against ship documents and the applicable codes.
Tank sounding is the determination of liquid level in ship tanks to calculate the volume and mass of contents. Two main measurement parameters exist: sounding — the distance from the tank bottom to the liquid surface, and ullage — the distance from the tank top to the liquid surface. The relationship is: sounding + ullage = tank height.
In practice, ballast tanks are usually measured by sounding while fuel tanks are measured by ullage. Manual measurement is performed using a sounding tape or sounding rod lowered through a sounding pipe. The tape must be certified and marked at every centimetre.
